research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is near-continuous (97.7% non-zero) with moderate CV (0.293), making a continuous-review (r,Q) policy well-suited. The large EOQ relative to MOQ(63) favours large, infrequent replenishments to minimise ordering costs. Safety stock is sized using the combined demand-and-lead-time variance formula at z=1.645 for 95% service level.
research_insights.boundary_risk: The storage cap of 841 units fully constrains the order quantity to 726 (down from unconstrained EOQ of ~1039). This reduces ordering frequency efficiency by ~28% vs. the true EOQ, increasing annual ordering costs. Any upward revision to safety stock (e.g. under higher demand volatility) would require either a warehouse capacity increase or a reduction in order quantity below EOQ-optimal.
